explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/600, whose remark reads 'Ruzsa and Szemerédi [RuSz78] proved that e(n,r)=o(n^2) for any fixed r', where e(n,r) is minimal such that every graph on n vertices with at least e(n,r) edges, each edge in at least one triangle, has an edge in at least r triangles. The Lean eFunction n r is sInf of the e for which Erdos600Prop n e r holds; Erdos600Prop quantifies over SimpleGraph (Fin n) with edge count ≥ e and every edge in a triangle (trianglesContaining = 3-cliques containing both endpoints), concluding some edge lies in ≥ r triangles. The set is upward closed and nonempty (e = C(n,2)+1 holds vacuously), so sInf is a genuine minimum bounded by C(n,2)+1. The theorem states, for every r, eFunction(·, r) = o(n^2) along atTop, exactly the cited result; for r = 0, 1 it is trivial (e = 1) and harmless. Faithful.
